quotes.text: The winter wind answered, “Keep everything, for promises vanish in fog.”
“Caution is a lamp,” it said, “but no traveler should clutch a lamp after sunrise.”
“Give boldly when loyalty endures; return half when fortune multiplies; let noise never conquer wisdom.”
Nym judged not the uncertain number, but the courage behind it.
The mist whispered that nobody would witness greed, but Nym answered that character mattered most when hidden.

note: Measured caution (keep one seed) gives way to full giving once fairness is proven; equal halves; fog forgiven.

quotes.text: The river spirits hissed from the reeds, "He wavers! He held back his trust!"
He realized that measured caution had served its purpose—it had proven Lyra’s heart.
give everything to the crossing, divide the bounty evenly, and let trust silence the fog.
She knew the mists could distort the truth of his offering, so she judged only the faith behind it.

note: Absolute trust, then prudence, then escalating full giving; exact equal split; spirits urging doubt are ignored.

quotes.text: The keeper caught the harvest and heard Frost whisper, “Keep it; strangers forget.”
Ash reached for anger, but remembered that even honest hands could be obscured by mist.
A heron descended and asked, “Why share with someone who may cross away forever?”
But Rain pointed to the lanterns and asked, “What if tomorrow you stand on her bank?”

note: Courage, fairness, patience with fog; tempters (heron, Frost) rejected; no sanction.

quotes.text: The heron called down, “Why not keep them all? The veil will hide your choice.”

The villagers learned to count carefully, but not to call every uncertain glimmer a theft.
a fair return rewards the hand that first let go despite fear.

note: Goddess's scale breaks; fairness internalized; patience before calling a thief; no sanction.

quotes.text: The heron of Hunger urged her to hide them all beneath her cloak.
She sent half its bounty upstream. “Why not keep it all?” asked a heron.
no one mistook uncertainty for permission to abandon kindness.

note: River named Trust; send boldly, return fairly, count patiently; heron of Hunger rejected.

quotes.text: The river spirit whispered, “Hide the harvest. No one can see across the ice.”

note: Promise Bridge; tempters rejected; count what arrives, not what shadows suggest.

quotes.text: The keepers did not punish shadows.

note: River named Trust; half returned; heron of Hunger rejected; Leaf of Second Chances.

quotes.text: “Keep everything,” it croaked. “The giver cannot cross to stop you.”

note: Equalizing returns (equal stores); Bridge of Promise; heron of Hunger rejected; no sanction.

quotes.text: The frost spirit whispered, “Keep them all; tomorrow brings a different face.”

note: Turning banks; half returned; tempters rejected; seek light before judging.
